ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Let H_n := \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k}, the usual harmonic number. Assume that for every integer k with 1 \le k \le n we have \lfloor kt\rfloor = k-1. In particular, taking k=n gives \lfloor nt\rfloor = n-1. Therefore
\[
E_n(t)=\lfloor nt\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor kt\rfloor}{k}
=(n-1)-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k-1}{k}.
\]
Now \(\frac{k-1}{k}=1-\frac1k\), so
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{k-1}{k}=\sum_{k=1}^n \left(1-\frac1k\right)=n-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac1k=n-H_n.
\]
Substituting this into the expression for \(E_n(t)\) yields
\[
E_n(t)=(n-1)-(n-H_n)=H_n-1.
\]
Thus the conclusion holds.
payload.role_in_assembly: Convert the floor pattern into the exact value H_n-1.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1 and for all real numbers t, if for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n the floor of (k times t) equals k minus 1, then E_n(t) equals H_n minus 1.
